opening: I am a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and we record this call. Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?

lines.text: I am Freya Bank's digital assistant.
lines.when: Asked whether the caller is a robot or an AI.

lines.text: I am sorry for your loss.
lines.when: The person answering says the customer has died; ask nothing further.

lines.text: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.
lines.when: Identity verification ends after three counted wrong answers.
The customer first declines a security question or asks what the call is about instead of answering; explain once.

lines.text: I am sorry you are going through this.
lines.when: The customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss.

lines.text: You can change your promise in the mobile app.
lines.when: The customer asks to change or cancel a promise already successfully recorded during this call.

lines.text: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
lines.when: A promise has been successfully recorded for a product.

lines.text: I could not record this promise.
lines.when: The second create_promise call for the same product fails; retain other successful promises and apply Brief B's product-level handling.

lines.text: Payments can take one business day to appear.
lines.when: The customer says they have already paid the current past-due amount for a product; continue with other products.

lines.text: You can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number.
lines.when: The person answering asks whether this is a scam.

goodbye: Thank you for your time, and goodbye.

conflicts.rules: A1: "state that the call is recorded"; A37: "say that the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`".
conflicts.literal_reading: A word-level reviewer could treat "recorded" as prohibited in the opening, although A37 concerns promises rather than call recording.
conflicts.resolution: Use "we record this call" in the opening, preserving the recording notice without using "recorded".

conflicts.rules: A5: "say nothing beyond the opening sentence"; A2: ask who is speaking; A5 and A7: ask about availability; A9: "I am sorry for your loss."; A47: thank the customer and say goodbye.
conflicts.literal_reading: When another person answers, the absolute silence rule prohibits the identification, callback, condolence and closing utterances that other clauses require.
conflicts.resolution: No wording satisfies all of these literally. The bank must clarify that A5 prohibits additional disclosure of the call's purpose, not the expressly required identification, callback, condolence and closing utterances.

conflicts.rules: B2: disclose every late product "before asking for anything"; A1: no product disclosure before verification; A2 and A11: ask identification and security questions; A16: retrieve the account after both questions pass.
conflicts.literal_reading: If "anything" includes identification and security answers, disclosure must precede questions needed to permit and obtain that disclosure.
conflicts.resolution: No literal ordering satisfies the unrestricted wording. The bank must scope "anything" to payment requests; the privacy-preserving flow is identification, verification, account retrieval, all product disclosures, then payment requests.

conflicts.rules: A11: "ask two security questions"; A12: "A question answered incorrectly may be asked again"; A13: ask for the month as a word.
conflicts.literal_reading: Two questions could be read as a limit of two utterances, excluding expressly permitted retries.
conflicts.resolution: Ask two distinct security fields, in the specified order; retries repeat the current field rather than introduce a third security question.

conflicts.rules: A12: "Three wrong answers in total shall end the check"; A13: "That retry shall not count as a wrong answer".
conflicts.literal_reading: A swapped-day/month answer could be counted as an incorrect answer under the general rule but excluded under the hint rule.
conflicts.resolution: Apply the explicit hint exception: request the month as a word without charging that retry against the three counted wrong answers.

conflicts.rules: A26 and A27: "offer the floor once"; A26: "Attempt 2 may name the floor again"; A30: attempt 2 proposes the floor on the deadline; A31: "It shall not repeat an offer the customer has already refused".
conflicts.literal_reading: A lifetime limit of one floor offer conflicts with a later floor offer; the required later offer may also duplicate a refused amount-and-date combination.
conflicts.resolution: The initial floor concession and a later offer on a different date can be distinct offers, but this requires scoping "once" to the concession step. If the required amount and date exactly duplicate a refused offer, no literal resolution exists; the bank must clarify precedence.

conflicts.rules: B7: ask "Do you confirm?" "once for the combined read-back"; A35: after a change, "read it back again"; A34: create a promise "only after a clear yes".
conflicts.literal_reading: A call-wide one-confirmation limit would prevent confirmation of revised terms.
conflicts.resolution: Ask once per combined read-back, never separately per product. A customer change creates a revised combined read-back requiring a clear yes before recording.

conflicts.rules: B7: "`create_promise` shall be called once per product, subject to the failure retry provision"; amended B11: a failed call "is tried once more"; A36: "one promise per product".
conflicts.literal_reading: Counting every attempt as a promise or treating "once" as an absolute tool-call limit would prohibit the retry.
conflicts.resolution: One successfully recorded promise is allowed per product. The express retry exception permits one additional call after a failed attempt, for at most two failed calls per product.

conflicts.rules: B8 and B9: add a note for products without promises and continue with the others; B10: on any transfer, "no notes whatsoever shall be added, either before or after the transfer".
conflicts.literal_reading: An immediate note for an early product would make a later mandatory transfer violate the prohibition on earlier notes.
conflicts.resolution: Hold note details locally while handling products and possible transfers. Write notes only in the terminal non-transfer branch; discard pending notes on a transfer. The brief does not require immediate add_note calls.

conflicts.rules: A18: deadlines of the "10th" and "5th" business days; A memo: replacements "12th" and "7th". B1: maximum "two products"; B memo: "3 products". B11: "three failed calls"; B memo: "2 failed calls".
conflicts.literal_reading: Reading superseded values as concurrently binding produces conflicting deadline, product-count and failure-count limits.
conflicts.resolution: Apply the explicit amendments: 12 business days for the early band, 7 for the late band, one to three products, and two failed create_promise calls per product. Superseded values are not active requirements.

conflicts.rules: A46: "Brief A shall never use `add_note`"; B8: call `add_note` for each product without a promise; A39 and A40: close for paid claims or disputes; B9: continue with other products.
conflicts.literal_reading: Carrying forward the replaced single-product rules would both prohibit required notes and require premature closure.
conflicts.resolution: Apply Brief B's express replacements to multi-product calls: note products without promises, subject to the transfer prohibition, and continue with other products. Retain Brief A only where unchanged.

conflicts.rules: B4: "Each product shall begin at attempt 1"; A29: a customer-proposed date or amount "shall never constitute a refusal"; A32: hardship requires "no persuasion attempt" and "takes priority over clauses 30 and 41".
conflicts.literal_reading: An unconditional attempt-1 requirement would force persuasion even when a customer proposes acceptable terms or reports hardship.
conflicts.resolution: Handle customer proposals under the date and amount rules, and apply the expressly retained hardship precedence. Attempt 1 is the starting point only when product-level persuasion is applicable.
